newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares look up, lack funds for growth spurt.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares look up, lack funds for growth spurt.

text.p: Leading Russian shares looked mostly firmer on continuing demand in morning trade on Tuesday, traders said. But they differed on where the market was headed for the day, although they ruled out any sharp moves.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index was little changed at 365.90 after closing on Monday at 365.64.
"The market is at a balance point and is fluctuating on this level," said Rinaco Plus trader Valery Levit.
"The direction now is up, but some prices are a litte too high. It's possible there will be a correction maybe even today or tomorrow."
He said leading oil companies, which have appreciated strongly recently, could correct down soon.
LUKoil LKOH.RTS slipped to $15.67 at at 0845 GMT after closing at $15.69 on Monday, while Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS firmed to $0.9530 from $0.9475.

He said international long-distance provider Rostelekom could also slip, citing unexceptional 1996 financial results and the transfer of a controlling stake to holding company Svyazinvest. Rostelekom RTKM.RTS eased to $3.85 from $3.87.
But Kirill Maltsev, head of institutional sales at Rye Man and Gor Securities said the market would continue to grow, if slowly, on Tuesday.
"I think there will be growth (today) because there hasn't been the kind of growth that would justify a correction," Maltsev said.
"The market is very strong -- it is standing just before the situation where it ought to break through to a new level."
But he said new investors were not yet bringing in enough funds to power the growth spurt, despite what he said was agressive buying on the second tier by long-time investors.
"On the second tier they're buying practically everything," he said. "Blue chips are very strong, but for now I don't see the aggressiveness."

He said markets in the West were still gathering steam after slowing down last month on fears U.S. interest rates would be raised, while uncertainty in the Russian economy over budget cuts and the new 1998 budget were also playing their part.
